Modern.brandNameRationale: Per Henrik Ling (1776–1839) is the documented Swedish physiologist who systematized what became Swedish massage at the Royal Gymnastic Central Institute in Stockholm (founded 1813). 'Fold' is a soft-tissue term for the layered release of fascia and muscle. Ling died in 1839; the surname is in the public domain when attached to a tradition word.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern massage brands have split into wellness-tech apps (Zeel, Soothe) and boutique studio chains (Massage Envy, Heyday). The opening is for a modern studio brand sited on the documented Swedish-massage lineage — clean, clinical-adjacent, but warm.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Heyday (heydayskincare.com) is the modern boutique peer, but skin-led. Zeel (zeel.com) holds the on-demand modern slot. Massage Envy (massageenvy.com) is the broad-market institutional middle. We sit closer to Heyday with a Swedish-tradition specialism.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern massage studio built on the Swedish line.

Luxury.tagline: The Swedish line, in the Parisian register.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Per Henrik Ling (1776–1839) founded the Royal Gymnastic Central Institute in Stockholm in 1813 and codified what became Swedish massage. 'Maison' places the brand in the Parisian luxury frame (Maison Margiela, Maison Goyard convention). Ling died in 1839; the surname is in the public domain. The pairing reads as a small Right-Bank treatment house.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury massage sits inside hotel spas (Aman, Four Seasons) or independent ateliers (Biologique Recherche treatment rooms). The opening is for a stand-alone luxury treatment house with documented Swedish-tradition roots — a Parisian register, not a hotel-spa register.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Biologique Recherche (biologique-recherche.com) holds the Parisian treatment-house peer slot. La Mer (cremedelamer.com) plays the heritage luxury reference. The Aman Spa (aman.com) sits in the hotel-spa luxury middle. We belong with Biologique Recherche, stand-alone and treatment-led.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A Parisian treatment house in the Swedish line, by appointment.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Per Henrik Ling (1776–1839) is the documented founder of Swedish massage. 'Co.' is the smallest commercial suffix — a single-word surname plus the trade tag. The brand names the tradition and stops there.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most massage brands accumulate menus — hot stones, aromatherapy, cupping, sound baths. There's an opening for a brand that offers one modality in one room at one price.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most boutique studios fail this purity test. The closest peers in spirit are some single-room Japanese shiatsu shops and certain old-school physiotherapy practices.
Minimal.positioningStatement: One modality. One room. One price.

targetAudience.primary: Clients who already know they want Swedish massage and want the time, the cost, and the booking link.

Minimal.logoDirection: Ling Co. set in a single-weight grotesque, lowercase. The mark appears on the door, the receipt, and nowhere else.

typography.rationale: One face. The door, the receipt, the booking page share the same mark.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Meridian references the documented shiatsu meridian system codified by Tokujiro Namikoshi (1905–2000) at the Japan Shiatsu College. As a brand anchor for a clinical bodywork operator, it signals serious manual-therapy depth. 'Group' follows the heritage clinical naming convention (Mayo Clinic, Cleveland Clinic).
Corporate.industrySummary: Clinical bodywork — manual therapy supplied to corporate wellness programs, insurance networks, and orthopedic referrals — is a B2B category dominated by mid-tier operators (Massage Envy Franchising, Hand & Stone). The opening is a mid-tier operator with multi-clinic capacity and insurance-grade reliability.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Hand & Stone (handandstone.com) holds the mid-tier clinical peer slot. Massage Envy (massageenvy.com) is the broad-market institutional middle. Athletico (athletico.com) plays the clinical PT peer. We sit closer to Athletico with a manual-therapy specialism.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Clinical manual therapy supplied to corporate wellness and orthopedic referral.

Creative.tagline: A bodywork house for the long undoing.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Pink Tiger evokes the California-Esalen wellness era (Big Sur, 1962 onward) without using the trademarked 'Esalen' name. Pink for warmth and skin; Tiger for the body's strength under release. The pairing reads as a warm, character-driven bodywork house with a Californian register.
Creative.manifesto: Most massage brands sell the hour. We sell the undoing. The week after the session. The breath that finally lengthens at minute forty. The shoulder that drops two inches on the drive home. The brand is for the long undoing, not the quick fix.
Creative.industrySummary: Massage branding has been clinical, sterile, and a little cold. There's room for one that's warm, narrative, character-driven, and serious about the slow release.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Heyday (heydayskincare.com) holds the modern boutique peer slot. Zeel (zeel.com) does the on-demand institutional middle. Olympia Wellness (olympiawellness.com) sits in the boutique-spa peer position. We sit warmer and more body-focused than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A bodywork house for the long undoing.
